name: grammar
title: A human-interpretable grammar as a pluggable rule engine
description: viva-grammar reimplements the cell-behavior hypothesis grammar (Johnson, Bergman, …, Fertig & Macklin, Cell 2025) as a process-bigraph module. The engine is ABM-agnostic; host coupling lives in thin adapters. This investigation's first study proves the engine on the paper's own hypoxia example; a follow-on will wire the blueprint adapter into viva-multicell-blueprint's CPM / vertex / center-based ABMs.
question: Can the Macklin/PhysiCell cell-behavior hypothesis grammar be implemented as a generic, ABM-agnostic process that reproduces published multicellular dynamics and plugs into different agent-based models unchanged?
hypothesis: A clean-room engine that compiles the grammar's rules to the paper's Hill-function mathematics, reading abstract per-cell signals and emitting abstract behaviors, can both (a) reproduce the paper's hypoxia → motility model on a minimal reference substrate and (b) drop into the MISM blueprint's MechanicsBackend in place of its built-in RulesProcess.

executive.what_is_this: A reusable implementation of a plain-text language for cell behavior. You write rules like "In tumor cells, oxygen decreases transformation to motile tumor," and the engine turns per-cell signals into per-cell behaviors each timestep — independent of which agent-based model provides the cells.
executive.verdict: The grammar engine reproduces the paper's transient post-hypoxic migration end-to-end on a minimal reference substrate, with all four acceptance bands met.
executive.verdict_detail: Study hypoxia-motility: peak motile fraction ≈ 0.34 (≥ 0.15), invasive-plume ratio ≈ 1.40× (≥ 1.2), reversion to 0.00 after reoxygenation (≤ 0.02), central necrotic core throughout. The engine ran as a separate process wired only through abstract signal/behavior ports.
decisions_needed: Stage 2 target: wire BlueprintGrammarProcess into a GRAMMAR-SHAPED blueprint study (confirmed with the MISM-blueprint session that per_step gives exact RulesProcess parity and the grammar replaces — not coexists with — the single rules slot). The grammar cannot reproduce the Sego flu model, which relies on ordered/resistance chaining; see docs/stage2-blueprint-integration.md.

scientific_argument.main_claim: The cell-behavior hypothesis grammar can be realized as a generic rule engine that reproduces published dynamics and is portable across agent-based models.
evidence_for: The hypoxia study reproduces the paper's qualitative dynamics on all four bands.
The engine math matches hand-computed Hill values and the verbatim hypoxia rule parameters (29 passing tests).
BlueprintGrammarProcess emits exactly the blueprint RulesProcess port surface (fates / scalar / divisions / deaths), so it is a structural drop-in.
evidence_against: The reference substrate is a toy (reduced oxygen diffusivity); it demonstrates the grammar, not quantitative tumor biology.
The grammar combines rules independently per (cell_type, behavior) — no rule ordering or scalar-chaining — so it cannot express ordered/resistance rule chains.
key_figures: workspace/studies/hypoxia-motility/viz/hypoxia_motility.html — oxygen field + cell cohort animation with the induction / plume / reversion dynamics.
caveats: Stage-2 blueprint integration is scaffolded but not yet wired into the live ABMs.

The grammar swap will NOT reproduce the Sego influenza blueprint, which relies on RulesProcess's ordered rules + resistance-scalar chaining; it is a drop-in only for grammar-shaped blueprints. (Confirmed against blueprint source, 2026-11-06.)
